questions.q: Why were horses like Beauty, handsome and high-bred, at the fair with the middle class of horses?
choices: Some accident or blemish had lowered them
They were still too young to be sold
They had never been broken in or trained
Their owners were moving abroad and needed quick money
questions.evidence: fallen into the middle class, through some accident or blemish

questions.q: Why were the broken-down old horses "sad sights" for Beauty?
choices: He knew he might end up in the same state one day
They were old friends he had known at Birtwick
They were blocking his view of the buyers
They kept making too much noise all day
questions.evidence: who knows not but he may come to the same state

questions.q: What did Beauty say there was a lot of at the horse fair?
choices: Lies and trickery
Good food and water
Kind, gentle grooms
Horse racing and betting
questions.evidence: there were more lies told and more trickery at that horse fair

questions.q: Why did the gentlemen always turn away from Beauty?
choices: They saw his broken knees
He was too small for a carriage
He tried to bite their hands
His price was much too high
questions.evidence: The gentlemen always turned from me when they saw my broken knees

questions.q: How did Beauty judge the buyers who came to look at him?
choices: By how they handled and treated him
By how much money they offered
By the fine clothes they wore
By how loudly they talked to the salesman
questions.evidence: I judged a good deal of the buyers by their manners to myself

questions.q: Besides his gentle way, what else made Beauty take to the gray-eyed man?
choices: His clean, fresh smell, like a hayloft
His fine gentleman's clothes and hat
His loud and cheerful laughing voice
The red apple he held out in his hand
questions.evidence: a fresh smell as if he had come out of a hayloft

questions.q: What did Beauty do when the gray-eyed man came back?
choices: Reached out his head toward him
Turned his back on him and stamped
Reared up in fear and pulled away
Neighed loudly for the salesman
questions.evidence: I could not help reaching out my head toward him

questions.q: What price did the gray-eyed man finally pay for Beauty?
choices: Twenty-four ten
Twenty-three pounds
Twenty-five pounds
Thirty pounds

questions.q: Some old horses at the fair looked "dejected." What does "dejected" mean here?
choices: Sad and hopeless
Proud and lively
Fat and very lazy
Young and wild

questions.q: How does the chapter end for Beauty?
choices: He goes to a kind family in London, hoping to be happy
He is sold to the hard-faced man with the loud voice
He is left unsold at the fair and sent back to Bath
He is sent home to Earlshall to work in the fields
questions.evidence: thinking I was going to be happy
